# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b83 — Never disconnect an operating appliance

Beta83 is a focused hardware-safety fix building on the tested Beta82 passive PID learning release. It protects an optional, explicitly selected **upstream power switch** from being turned OFF while its downstream device is working, and enforces an idle cooldown of **at least one full minute after the device stops**.

## Upstream switch OFF protection

- The switch stays ON while any managed native source is operating or reports an active `hvac_action` (heating, cooling, drying, fan, defrosting, preheating, or another non-idle activity). Even `state: off` cannot override contradictory native activity feedback.
- The controller requires **all native endpoints to report OFF or a genuine 0% proportional output**, no pending native command or owned ON output, no new environmental demand, and valid switch ownership before starting the cooldown.
- **At least 60 seconds of continuously verified idle** must elapse before the physical supply may switch OFF. The configurable `power_switch_cooldown_seconds` retains its existing **600-second (10-minute) default** and may be raised; it cannot weaken the new hard 60-second minimum.
- Any renewed operation, changed demand, unknown/unavailable source, missing capabilities, paused relay or missing supply feedback cancels the idle interval, so a later idle observation starts a fresh cooldown.
- After restarting Home Assistant, an upstream OFF cannot be authorized without at least another 60 seconds of controller observation. Previously persisted confirmed ON/OFF dwell timestamps remain authoritative where applicable.
- Before sending `switch.turn_off`, the physical device's safety state is rechecked after saving the intent and again immediately before dispatch. Newly resumed activity, revoked permissions or changed switch identity prevents the command.
- Device-specific minimum supply ON and OFF dwell limits, sleep/window policies, user/manual override protections and existing offline re-arming behavior are preserved. HEM never power-cycles a device to diagnose a fault.

This only applies to an upstream switch that the user has explicitly selected for a managed device. No outlet is assigned automatically, no existing controller is enabled, and HEM does not infer physical idleness from absent telemetry.

## Verification

- Dedicated regression tests cover all active HVAC actions, secondary outputs, unavailable states, 60-second minimum and longer configured cooldowns, activity interrupting the idle timer, restart protection, and state changes during a pending switch command.
- The earlier Beta64–82 switch ownership, device minimum ON/OFF, restart history, PID, room occupancy, window/sleep, localization, HA event and browser tests remain part of the version-gated release suite.
- The GitHub release and downloadable HACS ZIP are published only after the release workflow passes against the exact release-branch commit. CI uses simulated Home Assistant services; physical operation on a particular appliance should still be observed after installation.

## Installation

Update the existing Home Environment Manager integration through HACS to **v0.6.0b83**, restart Home Assistant, and refresh the dashboard. Keep your previously configured per-device power switch and cooldown; the default remains 10 minutes. A shorter cooldown down to 60 seconds is possible in the device's settings, subject to any stricter hardware minimum-ON/OFF protection. Your existing room, PID, presence, sleep, shade and device settings are retained.
